Intel cratered 28.6% after guiding Q4 revenue to a range of $15 billion to $16 billion, below what it just reported, briefly pulling QQQ into correction territory intraday.

Apple surpassed NVIDIA as the most valuable company at $5 trillion while Amazon CEO Andy Jassy pledged roughly $220 billion in 2026 capital spending.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and NVIDIA didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat NVDA. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

The Nasdaq-100 spent part of Friday, October 30, 2026, below the line that defines a correction, then climbed back above it before the close. It fell 3.46% to close at 28,384.85, after reaching an intraday low of 28,093.24.

Who is Danny / Shutterstock.com

That low sat 10.0% below the October 6 record close of 31,224.47. A correction means a 10% drop from a record, so the index crossed that line during the session. It closed 9.1% below the record, which means it never finished a day in correction.

Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) closed at $690.49, down 3.47%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.86% to 25,437.00, its lowest close since July 31.

The selling started in chips. Shares of Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) fell 28.6% after it guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15 billion to $16 billion, below the $16.5 billion it had just reported. Joe Tigay, a portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, said, "We're moving out of the hopes and dreams phase of the AI trade and into the 'show me' phase."

Why the Close Matters More Than the Intraday Low

The correction label is based on closing prices, and buyers came in before the close and raised the index back above the line. Volatility followed the same path. The VIX, which measures how much investors expect the S&P 500 to swing, hit 23.93 during the session but closed at 19.41, up 12.91%.

Meanwhile, costs to protect the debt of numerous U.S. technology heavyweights against default hit fresh record highs Friday. The protection price for Intel bonds for five years surged as much as 22.4 basis points Friday morning to 127.9 basis points a year, Bloomberg reported.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield remained below the 5.00% threshold for the second straight week. The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield remained largely unchanged at 5.31% for the week ending Oct. 30.

Unusual Machines operates as a parts supplier, not a platform builder, but one customer accounted for 42% of its Q2 revenue.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Red Cat Holdings didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat RCAT. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Drone defense stocks are among the hardest-hit corners of a risk-off market. Unusual Machines (NYSEAMERICAN:UMAC) stock trades at $15.27, down 12% on the day. That compares with a $17.28 close for Unusual Machines on October 29.

mailfor / iStock via Getty Images

Red Cat Holdings (NASDAQ:RCAT) stock is at $4.56, down 10%. Ondas Inc. (NASDAQ:ONDS) stock is at $6.29, down 9%. AeroVironment (NASDAQ:AVAV) stock is at $126.79, down 6%.

The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ), which tracks the NASDAQ 100, is down 4% amid this week's Big Tech earnings fallout. Speculative growth stocks typically fall harder than the market on days like this because their valuations rest largely on profits expected years from now.

Why High-Beta Drone Stocks Drop First When Fear Rises

On volatile days, traders tend to sell high-beta stocks (shares that swing more than the market) and richly valued or unprofitable names first. Defense-tech small caps like Unusual Machines get no pass even when their end markets look strong, with Unusual Machines, Red Cat and Ondas each pairing rapid growth with ongoing losses as they scale production.

AeroVironment holds the other end of the group as a larger defense prime guiding to positive generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) earnings for fiscal 2027. That profile helps explain why AeroVironment's decline is the smallest of the four.
